Thanks again for the time earlier, Jane — really helpful call and great context on the triage goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

Summary from our call:
- Primary goal: deploy a conversational assistant for clinicians to surface patient history and guideline references with high fidelity (low hallucination).
- Non-functional targets: p95 latency <= 200ms for single-turn queries, baseline throughput target ~120 req/s, and TCO-sensitive (looking to keep inference spend below $X/10k monthly for pilot).
- Data sensitivity: PHI will be redacted for the initial eval; longer-term private deployment + KMS expected.

What we'll send you next (today):
1) Recommended model candidates and why we think they fit (incl. cheaper 13B option for latency-sensitive paths)
2) Prompt sets we used in the call (attached: acme_eval_prompt_set_v1.txt) and an initial tradeoff matrix for quantization approaches (attached)
3) Proposed test plan: run an AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 throughput/quality trade study on a 1k sample set you provide (redacted) and report EM/F1/ROUGE + latency/cost metrics

Ask: Can you confirm you can share a redacted sample set (500–1,000 prompts) and whether we should route test data to Redwood Hosted or Private (VPC) for the eval? We can run tests under an NDA and on Private if PHI is still a concern.

Next steps I propose:

- Run trade study (AWQ/GPTQ/FP8) and share results + recommended model + quantization profile

I've attached the prompt set and an initial AWQ/GPTQ tradeoff matrix for your review. If this sounds good I'll get Neha to schedule the deep-dive with your technical contact.

Hi Jane — Neha from Redwood SE here. Following up with a more technical checklist and our recommended candidates for the eval.

Quick recommendations (starting point):
- 70B instruction-tuned (Llama-3-70B-Chat) — best chance for highest quality; expected to require AWQ or high-fidelity GPTQ to preserve correctness at lower bits.
- 30B MPT-family (MPT-30B-Instruct) — good midpoint: lower cost, solid instruction-following. Likely tolerates GPTQ in many workloads.
- 13B instruction-tuned (e.g., T5x/Redwood-13B-Inst) — fallback for latency-sensitive endpoints; less likely to meet the highest fidelity bar but much cheaper.

Notes on quantization options and expected impact: 
- AWQ: generally preserves distributional properties and often shows smaller degradation on factuality/QA EM metrics compared to naive GPTQ at same bit width. Good first pass when quality is critical.
- GPTQ: faster turnaround and widely-supported, but we often see higher variance on long-tail outputs and subtle tokenization artifacts that can increase hallucination in open-ended prompts.
- FP8 (NVIDIA FP8 kernels / hardware FP8): biggest potential throughput win on supported stacks (up to 2–3x throughput), but risk of slight increases in calibration/hallucination; requires careful calibration and sometimes per-layer scaling.

Proposed trade study rubric (what we'll measure):
- Quality: Exact Match / F1 on the curated question set, ROUGE-L for long-form answers, calibration/hallucination spot checks on clinical prompts
- Performance: latency (p50/p95), throughput (tokens/s and req/s), and GPU memory footprint
- Cost: per-1k-requests cost estimates across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Plan: run AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 across the three model sizes above on your sample (1k prompts), provide a one-page summary with the recommended production configuration and a confident fallback strategy.

I'll start the internal job ticket as soon as we have the sample and confirmation on hosting environment. If you prefer, we can run a small 100-prompt pilot first to validate the pipeline and preserve the rest of your sample.

Links: benchmark dashboard (internal) — https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3CExampleDriveLink (I will drop the run config and results here)

Hi Jane — great questions, answers inline below.

1) Hosting for the eval: we can run the eval on Redwood Hosted under a restricted project with data retention disabled for the run, or run inside your Private (VPC) environment if you prefer. Given PHI concerns we typically recommend Private for anything that could be re-identifiable; Hosted is fine if you can guarantee redaction and your security team is OK with short-lived retention disabled. We will not retain the raw sample after the test — we can add that to an MSA addendum and we'll only persist aggregate metrics and run logs.

2) Sample size: we recommend a 500–1,000 prompt set for the main run. For quick validation, a 100-prompt smoke test is helpful. Statistically, 500 gives good power for EM/F1 differences across quantization choices for typical clinical QA prompts.

3) Pricing delta (ballpark for pilot):
- Hosted: pay-as-you-go; lower up-front but per-token cost higher. Estimated pilot cost: ~$3k–5k depending on run depth.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity; you'd commit to a month of reserved GPUs — higher commitment but lower per-token cost (best for production).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): platform + infra cost; varies by customer. For pilots we offer a time-limited Private eval credit and can scope a short-term Dedicated pilot if you want to replicate production latency.

Next steps / ask:
- If you can share the 800 redacted prompts, we'll start with a 100-prompt smoke test (Hosted or Private per your comfort) then proceed to full 800-run AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 study.
- Can you share procurement contact so we can route any pilot contract/NDAs?

I'll have Neha schedule the tech deep-dive for sometime tomorrow if that works for you.

Best,
Marissa
